specification.title: GVE Level 3 Plugin and Action Contracts

summary: GVE Level 3 Plugin and Action Contracts defines application-independent plugin and action contracts, deterministic sealed registry snapshots, operation interpretation, immutable plan-candidate binding, and exactly one fresh uniquely attributable contract production for each governed operation. It distinguishes replay from regeneration and preserves plugin and action ownership of application-specific meaning.

definitions.text: The application-independent contract enforced by the core for one plugin, including stable plugin identity, compatible plugin-interface version, one plugin-owned action registry, and the common facts needed for deterministic registration and resolution without exposing action-specific meaning.

The application-independent contract enforced by an owning plugin for one action, including stable action identity, compatible action-interface version, one declared input contract, and the common capabilities required to interpret and contract one governed operation.
The explicit association of one plugin identity and common plugin contract with the core-owned plugin registry before that registry is validated and sealed.
The explicit association of one action identity and common action contract with exactly one owning plugin's action registry before that registry is validated and sealed.
The core-owned deterministic resolution of one requested plugin identity to exactly one compatible registered plugin using only application-independent plugin-registry facts.
The selected-plugin-owned deterministic resolution of one requested action identity to exactly one compatible registered action in that plugin's sealed action registry.

The complete action-owned declaration of required, optional, forbidden, and structurally constrained inputs for that action, together with the action-owned rules needed to interpret their application-specific meaning.

The application-independent determination that supplied input has the declared shape, presence, identity, and representation required by an action contract, without interpreting the application's semantic meaning.
The selected action's authoritative interpretation of its supplied inputs, governing authority, and requested operation meaning after structural conformance has been established.

The single fresh immutable contract output produced for one successfully interpreted operation and uniquely attributable to the immutable plan candidate, workflow, operation, selected plugin and action, interface versions, registry snapshots, governing authority, complete interpreted inputs, and contract-production identity that produced it.

The property that a validated operation contract is bound to the exact current immutable plan candidate and every operation, interpreted-input, plugin, action, interface, registry, authority, and production fact from which it was produced and has not been invalidated or superseded.

The fail-closed determination that a plugin or action registry is complete, deterministic, internally compatible, free of duplicate or conflicting identities, and suitable to become immutable for one planning and execution attempt.

A uniquely identifiable immutable snapshot of a validated plugin registry or action registry after which registration, replacement, identity mutation, and interface-version mutation are forbidden for the governed attempt.

The deterministic binding of exactly one validated operation contract to one immutable plan candidate and all identities, versions, snapshots, authority, interpreted inputs, and contract-production facts governing one operation.

The required binding of contract interpretation and production to one already existing immutable plan-candidate identity whose pre-contract facts include the operation, selected plugin and action, governing authority, and sealed registry snapshots.

A stable identity for one distinct production of a validated operation contract, bound to one plan candidate, operation, interpreted-input identity, and deterministic production ordinal or equivalent application-independent discriminator.

The selected action acting through its owning plugin as the sole authority that allocates a nonnegative signed-64-bit production ordinal for each distinct validated-contract production within one plan-candidate-and-operation production lineage. The allocator preserves prior allocations, returns the prior ordinal only for exact replay, assigns the least unused ordinal for regeneration, and fails closed rather than issuing a duplicate or ambiguous allocation.
Reuse of the exact same previously produced immutable validated contract and contract-production identity for the same unchanged plan candidate, without claiming a new production.
A new contract-production event for the same or successor plan candidate. Regeneration has a fresh contract-production identity and must not be represented as replay of a prior production.

requirements.text: Each governed operation must request exactly one nonempty plugin identity and exactly one nonempty action identity owned by that plugin; missing, multiple, conflicting, or ambiguous requested identities must fail closed.
Plugins must register only with the core-owned plugin registry through the common plugin contract, and each plugin identity must resolve to at most one compatible registered plugin.
Actions must register only with exactly one owning plugin's action registry through the common action contract and must not register directly with the core.
The core must complete deterministic plugin resolution before action resolution, and only the selected plugin may resolve the requested action from its own validated sealed action-registry snapshot.

The core may validate common plugin-contract identity, interface-version compatibility, registry attribution, and structural conformance, but must not interpret, derive, normalize, override, compare, or validate plugin-owned action or input meaning.
Each action must own one complete declared input contract and must retain authoritative application-specific interpretation of every supplied input and the requested operation meaning.

Structural input conformance must be evaluated before action interpretation; missing required input, forbidden input, duplicate input identity, malformed representation, or structural mismatch must fail closed without inventing action-specific meaning.

One successfully resolved and interpreted operation must produce exactly one fresh, valid, immutable, and uniquely attributable validated operation contract with one distinct contract-production identity; zero contracts, multiple contracts, reused contracts without explicit replay attribution, ambiguous productions, or non-unique attribution must fail closed.

Every validated operation contract must bind the current immutable plan-candidate identity, workflow identity, operation identity, plugin identity, action identity, plugin-interface version, action-interface version, plugin-registry snapshot identity, action-registry snapshot identity, governing authority, complete interpreted inputs, and contract-production identity.

A validated operation contract must be fresh for every fact to which it is bound; any change to the plan-candidate identity, operation content, interpreted inputs, selected plugin or action, interface version, registry snapshot, or governing authority must invalidate the prior contract for current acceptance and require fresh production.

Before a planning or execution attempt, the core-owned plugin registry and every participating plugin-owned action registry must be complete, validated, deterministic, sealed, uniquely identified, and immutable for that attempt.

Duplicate registration, late registration, unavailable identity, unauthorized registration, conflicting ownership, ambiguous resolution, identity mutation, incompatible interface version, incomplete registry validation, or registry snapshot drift must fail closed.

A missing, malformed, unauthorized, stale, incompatible, conflicting, duplicate, incomplete, or non-uniquely attributable validated operation contract must fail closed and must not be repaired by inference, fallback selection, or reuse.

Each action must have an independently identifiable source module and one explicit registration entry in its owning plugin; adding an action must not require core modification or modification to unrelated action implementations.

Registry validity, successful resolution, structural conformance, action interpretation, and validated-contract production establish no workflow-plan acceptance, operation eligibility, attempt, completion, observation, verification, effect, evidence sufficiency, or authoritative result claim.

This specification must not define workflow-plan states, dependency or handoff eligibility, attempt ordering, blocking, skipping, cancellation, timeout, lifecycle transitions, evidence schemas, effect-claim realization, operation-result schemas, uncertainty, or authoritative workflow-result assembly.

This specification must not define maintained runtime, plugin, action, registry, or executor implementation; language-specific interface syntax; exhaustive production action catalogs; plugin-specific credentials or publication semantics; production payload schemas; bootstrap executor formats; or changes to accepted Levels 0 through 2.

Contract freshness must bind to stable governed identities sufficient to detect relevant change, including immutable plan-candidate identity, operation content, selected plugin identity, selected action identity, governed instruction set revision, governing authority context, workflow-plan attempt, result-realization attempt, observation context, freshness boundary, sealed registry snapshots, interpreted inputs, and contract-production identity. Freshness must not depend on future acceptance success. Freshness must not be established by an unbound Boolean assertion.

Contract interpretation and production must begin only after one complete immutable plan-candidate identity exists. A contract must not bind to a future successful acceptance outcome, an accepted-plan identity not yet established, a mutable planning session, or an identity whose value depends on that contract.

Replay must retain the exact prior contract identity and contract-production identity and is valid only for the exact unchanged plan candidate and all bound freshness facts. Regeneration must create a fresh contract-production identity even when interpreted meaning is unchanged.

A missing, duplicate, conflicting, reused-as-new, ambiguous, stale, partial, unresolved, or circular plan-candidate or contract-production binding must fail closed and must not be repaired by inference, fallback, lifecycle state, or acceptance outcome.

The selected action, acting through exactly one owning plugin, is the sole contract-production ordinal allocator for each plan-candidate-and-operation production lineage. The uniqueness domain is the tuple of immutable plan-candidate identity and operation identity; within that domain every distinct production must have exactly one unique nonnegative signed-64-bit ordinal.

For a previously unseen production lineage, the first contract production must receive ordinal zero. Exact replay must retain the prior ordinal and contract-production identity. Regeneration must receive the least nonnegative ordinal not previously allocated in that lineage, even when interpreted meaning and contract content are otherwise unchanged. Allocation state must be evaluated against one immutable lineage snapshot.

Concurrent or repeated production requests must not yield the same new ordinal. A duplicate allocation, reused-as-new ordinal, skipped or conflicting prior allocation history, ordinal outside the nonnegative signed-64-bit domain, exhausted domain, ambiguous lineage, or inability to establish one immutable allocation snapshot must fail closed without contract production or acceptance.
